claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can be used to determine whether a material has a ferromagnetic ground state.
The determination can be made by comparing the total energies of spin-polarized ferromagnetic and non-spin-polarized configurations.
Enabling spin polarization in DFT allows the electrons to adopt a spin-ordered state.
The calculations represent ideal structural conditions at 0 K and zero external magnetic field.
Spin polarization changes the electron density and produces exchange splitting in the electronic density of states.
Exchange interactions can lower the total energy by splitting the spin-up and spin-down bands.
An energy minimum in a spin-polarized state indicates a ferromagnetic ground state.
The spin-polarized ferromagnetic configuration will have lower total energy than the non-spin-polarized configuration.
The spin-polarized configuration will have a nonzero magnetic moment.
Non-spin-polarized DFT predicts a higher-energy, magnetically disordered structure for the proposed material.
The approach is applicable to zero-temperature ground-state predictions.
The result may depend on the exchange-correlation functional and treatment of electronic correlations.
Zero-temperature DFT predictions may not reliably extrapolate to finite-temperature magnetic behavior.
DFT may inadequately capture strong electronic correlations in some materials.
Low-temperature SQUID magnetometry can test for a spontaneous magnetic moment.
